rules.title: Ban on coordinated pricing algorithms for rents
rules.requirement: It is illegal to sell rent-setting algorithms that use private competitor data to Berkeley landlords, and illegal for landlords to use them to set rents or occupancy levels. Each month and each unit is a separate violation.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 civil penalty per violation

coverage_conditions.text: Residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley. Covers any process using nonpublic competitor data (less than 90 days old) to recommend rents, fees, occupancy or lease terms; excludes aggregated anonymous reports, affordable-housing rent/income limit tools, and market research, appraisal, or software development uses.

rules.quoted_span:
B. It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley.
rules.requirement_es: Es ilegal vender a los propietarios de Berkeley algoritmos que usan datos privados de competidores para fijar rentas, y es ilegal que los propietarios los usen para fijar rentas o niveles de ocupación. Cada mes y cada unidad cuenta como una violación separada.

rules.title: Tenant screening fee rights statement required
rules.requirement: If a Berkeley landlord charges a screening or application fee, they must give you, before taking the fee, a written statement of your screening fee rights and the maximum fee allowed by state law.

coverage_conditions.text: Owners or agents in Berkeley who charge a fee to purchase a consumer credit report and process a rental application.

rules.quoted_span: When an owner or the owner’s agent gets a request to rent residential property in Berkeley from an applicant and the owner charges a fee to purchase a consumer credit report and to validate, review, or otherwise process an application, the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under
rules.requirement_es: Si un arrendador en Berkeley cobra una tarifa de evaluación o de solicitud, debe darle, antes de recibir la tarifa, una declaración escrita de sus derechos sobre la tarifa de evaluación y el monto máximo permitido por la ley estatal.

rules.title: No non-refundable fees to renew a tenancy or change roommates
rules.requirement: A Berkeley landlord cannot charge a current tenant a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy, including fees when a roommate leaves or when you ask to add or replace a roommate.

coverage_conditions.text: Existing tenants of residential rental property in Berkeley; applies regardless of contrary lease language.

rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.
rules.requirement_es: Un arrendador en Berkeley no puede cobrar a un inquilino actual una tarifa no reembolsable para renovar el arrendamiento, incluidas las tarifas cuando un compañero de casa se va o cuando usted pide agregar o reemplazar a un compañero.

rules.title: Relocation assistance for Ellis Act evictions
rules.requirement: If a landlord evicts you to take the property off the rental market (Ellis Act), the landlord must pay you the same relocation money as for an owner move-in eviction. Starting January 1, 2026, that is $19,413, plus $6,471 more for qualifying households.

coverage_conditions.text: Tenants evicted so the owner can remove the property from the rental housing market under Berkeley's Ellis Implementation Ordinance.

applies_if.source_text: eviction is to remove the property from the rental market (Ellis Act)

rules.quoted_span: The Ellis Implementation Ordinance requires the same relocation assistance payments for tenants evicted so the owner can remove a property from the rental housing market.
rules.requirement_es: Si el propietario lo desaloja para retirar la propiedad del mercado de alquiler (Ley Ellis), debe pagarle la misma ayuda de reubicación que en un desalojo para ocupación del propietario. Desde el 1 de enero de 2026, son $19,413, más $6,471 adicionales para hogares que califiquen.

rules.title: Just cause eviction (Measure BB changes)
rules.requirement: Tenants in fully or partially covered Berkeley units can only be evicted for a just cause. A tenant cannot be evicted for unpaid rent of less than one month's Fair Market Rent, or for refusing to sign a similar new lease.
rules.key_value: nonpayment eviction requires debt of at least one month's Fair Market Rent

coverage_conditions.text: Units fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance. Eviction notices must refer tenants to the Rent Board, and copies must be filed with the Rent Board within three business days of service.

rules.quoted_span: In Berkeley, tenants in units that are fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted unless there is "just cause” (previously called “good cause”).
rules.requirement_es: Los inquilinos de unidades de Berkeley con cobertura total o parcial solo pueden ser desalojados por una causa justa. No se puede desalojar a un inquilino por renta impaga menor a un mes de la Renta Justa de Mercado, ni por negarse a firmar un nuevo contrato similar.

rules.title: Relocation assistance for owner move-in evictions
rules.requirement: If a landlord evicts you so the owner can move in, the landlord must pay you relocation money. Starting January 1, 2026, the standard payment is $19,413, plus $6,471 more for qualifying households.

coverage_conditions.text: Tenants evicted for owner move-in under Berkeley's Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance.

applies_if.source_text: eviction is an owner move-in eviction

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance requires owners to pay tenants relocation assistance in the event of an owner move-in eviction.
rules.requirement_es: Si el propietario lo desaloja para mudarse a la unidad, debe pagarle una ayuda de reubicación. Desde el 1 de enero de 2026, el pago estándar es de $19,413, más $6,471 adicionales para hogares que califiquen.

rules.title: Berkeley 2026 Annual General Adjustment (1.0%)
rules.requirement: For 2026, eligible Berkeley landlords may raise rent ceilings on covered units by no more than 1.0%, starting no earlier than January 1, 2026. The yearly increase is set at 65% of the Bay Area inflation rate (CPI).

coverage_conditions.text: Eligible landlords of units with permanent rent ceilings under the Berkeley Rent Ordinance; conditions for qualifying are in Rent Board Regulation 1148.

exemptions.label: Tenancy began on or after January 1, 2025 with rent set under Costa-Hawkins

all.source_text: Tenancy began on or after January 1, 2025 and the rent was set pursuant to the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act

rules.exemptions: Tenancy began on or after January 1, 2025 with rent set under Costa-Hawkins
rules.quoted_span:
At its regular meeting on October 16, 2025, the Berkeley Rent Stabilization Board 
adopted the Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Order for Year 2026 which will allow 
eligible landlords to increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than 
January 1, 2026.
rules.requirement_es: Para 2026, los propietarios elegibles de Berkeley pueden aumentar los topes de renta de las unidades cubiertas en no más de 1.0%, a partir del 1 de enero de 2026 como muy pronto. El aumento anual se fija en el 65% de la inflación (IPC) del Área de la Bahía.

rules.title: Annual General Adjustment capped at 5% (Measure BB)
rules.requirement: In fully covered Berkeley units, rent can rise each year only by the Annual General Adjustment set by the Rent Board, which is tied to inflation and can be no more than 5%.

coverage_conditions.text: Fully covered units (rent ceiling): most units in multifamily properties built before 1980, single-family homes with tenancies that began before 1996, and single-family homes with five or more rooms rented separately. Partially covered (no rent ceiling): new construction with a certificate of occupancy issued after 1980, most single-family homes, and most condominiums. Government-owned or subsidized units are now fully or partially covered depending on unit type. Landlords with banked AGAs from prior years may still raise rent above 5% up to the rent ceiling.

exemptions.label: New construction (certificate of occupancy issued after 1980)
Most single-family homes and condominiums (partially covered)

all.source_text: single-family home with tenancy that began before 1996 or five or more rooms rented separately

rules.exemptions: New construction (certificate of occupancy issued after 1980); Most single-family homes and condominiums (partially covered)
rules.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%.
rules.requirement_es: En las unidades de Berkeley con cobertura total, la renta solo puede subir cada año según el Ajuste General Anual que fija la Junta de Renta, ligado a la inflación y que no puede ser mayor del 5%.

rules.title: Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance (criminal history)
rules.requirement: Landlords in Berkeley may not ask about or use criminal history or criminal background checks in ads, applications, tenant selection, or decisions. If a landlord acts based on criminal history where allowed, they must give written notice and a chance to respond.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to rental housing providers in Berkeley for current and prospective tenants. Exemptions (see ordinance for details): lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8; owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner of record lives in one unit; units rented under an agreement letting owners move back (BMC 13.76.130 A.9); existing tenants subletting or adding/replacing roommates.

exemptions.label: Owner-occupied property of 1-3 units

all.source_text: owner of record resides in one of the units as primary residence

exemptions.label: Owner move-back rental agreement

all.source_text: unit under a rental agreement allowing owner to move back per BMC 13.76.130 A.9

exemptions.label: Existing tenant sublet or roommate

all.source_text: existing tenant seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates

exemptions.label: Lifetime sex offender registrants

all.source_text: applicant is a lifetime sex offender registrant

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied property of 1-3 units; Owner move-back rental agreement; Existing tenant sublet or roommate; Lifetime sex offender registrants
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores en Berkeley no pueden preguntar ni usar antecedentes penales ni verificaciones de antecedentes penales en anuncios, solicitudes, selección de inquilinos o decisiones. Si un arrendador actúa por antecedentes penales cuando está permitido, debe dar aviso por escrito y la oportunidad de responder.

rules.title: Berkeley security deposit interest
rules.requirement: In Berkeley units fully or partly covered by the Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit every year, plus a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before year end.

coverage_conditions.text: Tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance.

applies_if.source_text: Unit fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance

rules.quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.
rules.requirement_es: En las unidades de Berkeley cubiertas total o parcialmente por la Ordenanza de Renta, los propietarios deben pagar a los inquilinos intereses sobre su depósito de seguridad cada año, más una cantidad prorrateada si el inquilino se muda antes de fin de año.

rules.title: RSO no-fault eviction relocation assistance
rules.requirement: For no-fault evictions from rent-stabilized (RSO) units in Los Angeles, the landlord must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD and pay relocation assistance within 15 days of the notice. For July 2026 to June 2027 the amounts range from $11,000 to $27,400 depending on tenancy length, income, and whether the tenant is qualified (62+, disabled, or with minor children).

coverage_conditions.text: No-fault evictions (owner/relative/manager occupancy, demolition or removal from rental use, government order to vacate, conversions, etc.) from units covered by the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance. Reduced amounts for Mom and Pop properties for owner/family occupancy evictions.

rules.quoted_span:
All tenant not- at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a 
Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) before 
evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause 
Ordinance (JCO).
rules.requirement_es: En desalojos sin culpa de unidades con renta estabilizada (RSO) en Los Ángeles, el propietario debe presentar una Declaración de Intención de Desalojo ante LAHD y pagar asistencia de reubicación dentro de 15 días del aviso. De julio de 2026 a junio de 2027 los montos van de $11,000 a $27,400 según la duración del arrendamiento, los ingresos y si el inquilino es calificado (62+ años, con discapacidad o con hijos menores).

rules.title: JCO no-fault eviction relocation assistance
rules.requirement: For no-fault evictions from units covered by the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO) in Los Angeles, the landlord must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD and pay relocation assistance within 15 days of the notice. Amounts range from $11,000 to $27,400 for July 2026 to June 2027, or one month's rent for certain single-family homes owned by individuals.
rules.key_value: $11,000–$27,400 per unit (July 1, 2026–June 30, 2027); one month's rent for single-family homes owned by natural persons

coverage_conditions.text: No-fault evictions from units covered by the Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance. Single-family dwellings owned by a natural person who owns no more than four units and a single-family home in the City pay one month's rent.

rules.quoted_span:
All tenant not- at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a 
Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) before 
evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause 
Ordinance (JCO).
rules.requirement_es: En desalojos sin culpa de unidades cubiertas por la Ordenanza de Causa Justa (JCO) en Los Ángeles, el propietario debe presentar una Declaración de Intención de Desalojo ante LAHD y pagar asistencia de reubicación dentro de 15 días del aviso. Los montos van de $11,000 a $27,400 de julio de 2026 a junio de 2027, o un mes de renta para ciertas casas unifamiliares de personas físicas.

rules.title: Resident Protections Ordinance relocation for demolition
rules.requirement: If a Los Angeles landlord demolishes a protected unit to build new housing, lower-income tenants must get enhanced relocation payments (for 2026-27, up to $115,480 under the standard option), and all tenants get at least the RSO or JCO amount.

coverage_conditions.text: Protected Units demolished for new construction within 5 years after filing the Notice of Intent to Withdraw or Declaration of Intent to Evict; Protected Units include all RSO units and units with recent affordability covenants, rent control, lower-income occupants, or Ellis Act withdrawal.

rules.quoted_span:
Owners who demolish a Protected Unit for the purpose of new construction within 5 years after the 
filing of the Notice of Intent to Withdraw or Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD are required to 
comply with relocation requirements under the RPO.
rules.requirement_es: Si un propietario en Los Ángeles demuele una unidad protegida para construir nueva vivienda, los inquilinos de bajos ingresos deben recibir pagos de reubicación mayores (para 2026-27, hasta $115,480 bajo la opción estándar), y todos los inquilinos reciben al menos el monto de RSO o JCO.

rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: In Los Angeles, most rental units not under rent control can only be ended for a legal reason listed in the law. If you are evicted for a no-fault reason, like the owner moving in, your landlord may have to pay you relocation money.

coverage_conditions.text: Most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the RSO, including single-family dwellings, once the tenant has lived in the unit 6 months or the original lease has expired, whichever comes first. Exceptions include transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity/sorority houses, owner's roommate, certain cooperatives, some non-profit homeless or substance-abuse facilities, and some HACLA or government-owned properties. Since March 27, 2023, tenants cannot be evicted for nonpayment unless they owe more than the Fair Market Rent for the unit size.

rules.title: RSO annual allowable rent increase (July 2025 - June 2026)
rules.requirement: For units covered by the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance, the yearly rent increase from July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026 is limited to 3%. Starting February 2, 2026, landlords can no longer add an extra percentage for utilities.

rules.title: Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) annual increase limit
rules.requirement: For rent-stabilized units, rent may go up only once every 12 months, by the allowable percentage set each year. When a tenant moves out voluntarily or is evicted for certain reasons, the rent can be reset to market rate.

Rent amount is not regulated for condo/townhome tenancies that began after December 31, 1995.

rules.title: Proposed ban on anti-competitive automated rent price-fixing
rules.requirement: This proposed ordinance would make it illegal to sell or license rent-setting software that uses private competitor data, and illegal for landlords to use it to set rents or occupancy levels. Tenants could sue for up to $1,000 per violation.

rules.title: Ban on algorithmic devices to set rents
rules.requirement: Landlords in San Francisco may not use, and companies may not sell, software that analyzes private competitor rent data to recommend rents or manage occupancy. Tenants or the City Attorney can sue over violations.

rules.quoted_span:

adding Section 37.10C to the Rent Ordinance went into effect on October 14, 2024. The law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco.

rules.title: Just cause required for evictions
rules.requirement: In units covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance, a landlord can only evict you for one of 17 listed just-cause reasons. The lease simply ending or a change in owner is not a just cause.

coverage_conditions.text: Rental units covered by the Rent Ordinance, including newer units (certificate of occupancy after June 13, 1979) and Costa-Hawkins units that are exempt from rent increase limits.

applies_if.source_text: rental unit is covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance eviction provisions

rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction.
rules.requirement_es: En unidades cubiertas por la Ordenanza de Alquiler de San Francisco, el propietario solo puede desalojarlo por una de 17 causas justas enumeradas. El simple vencimiento del contrato o un cambio de dueño no es causa justa.

rules.title: San Francisco annual allowable rent increase (3/1/2026-2/28/2027)
rules.requirement: For rent-controlled units in San Francisco, the most your landlord can raise your rent for the yearly increase from March 1, 2026 to February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.

rules.title: Santa Ana annual rent increase cap
rules.requirement: Your landlord can raise rent only once a year, by no more than 3% or 80% of the change in the Consumer Price Index, whichever is lower. From September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027, the maximum increase is 2.87%.

rules.title: Santa Ana rent stabilization cap
rules.requirement: In Santa Ana, rent can go up by no more than 3% per year or 80% of the change in CPI, whichever is lower. If CPI is negative, no rent increase is allowed.

rules.title: Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: In California, it is illegal to use or share a common pricing algorithm (software using competitor data to set or recommend prices or terms) as part of an agreement to restrain trade, or to pressure others to adopt its recommended prices or terms.

coverage_conditions.text: Any person (not end consumers) using or distributing a common pricing algorithm, meaning any methodology including software used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or influence a price or commercial term. Adds Bus. & Prof. Code §§ 16729 and 16756.1.

rules.quoted_span: (a) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
rules.requirement_es: En California, es ilegal usar o compartir un algoritmo de precios común (programa que usa datos de competidores para fijar o recomendar precios o condiciones) como parte de un acuerdo para restringir el comercio, o presionar a otros a adoptar sus precios o condiciones recomendados.

rules.title: Application screening fee cap, receipts and refunds
rules.requirement: A landlord can charge an application screening fee only to cover actual costs, and never more than $30 per applicant (adjusted each year for inflation). You must get an itemized receipt, a copy of your credit report, and a refund if no unit is available, your application is not considered, or the fee is not fully used.

coverage_conditions.text: Applicants for residential rental property, including guarantors and cosigners.

rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.
rules.requirement_es: El propietario solo puede cobrar una tarifa de evaluación de solicitud para cubrir los costos reales, y nunca más de $30 por solicitante (ajustado cada año por inflación). Debe recibir un recibo detallado, una copia de su informe de crédito y un reembolso si no hay unidad disponible, si su solicitud no se considera o si la tarifa no se usa por completo.

rules.title: Limits on criminal history screening (FEHA)
rules.requirement: Landlords may check criminal history but cannot consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and cannot ban everyone with a record. A denial must be based on a conviction directly related to being a good tenant.

coverage_conditions.text: Most housing providers and housing-related services in California, including landlords and tenant screening companies.

rules.quoted_span: Housing  providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system. Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
rules.requirement_es: Los propietarios pueden revisar antecedentes penales, pero no pueden considerar arrestos sin condena, registros sellados o borrados, ni registros juveniles, y no pueden rechazar a todas las personas con antecedentes. Un rechazo debe basarse en una condena directamente relacionada con ser un buen inquilino.

rules.title: Source of income discrimination ban (FEHA)
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot refuse to rent to you or treat you differently because of how you pay rent, including Section 8 vouchers or other rental assistance.

rules.title: Source-of-income discrimination ban and credit-history alternative
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot refuse or treat you differently because of your source of income, including Section 8 and other housing vouchers. If you have a rent subsidy, the landlord must base income tests on your share of the rent and let you show other proof of ability to pay instead of credit history.
rules.key_value: No source-of-income discrimination; alternative to credit history for subsidized applicants

rules.requirement_es: Los propietarios no pueden rechazarlo ni tratarlo de manera diferente por su fuente de ingresos, incluidos los vales de vivienda de la Sección 8 y otros. Si tiene un subsidio de renta, el propietario debe basar los requisitos de ingresos en su parte de la renta y permitirle mostrar otra prueba de capacidad de pago en lugar de su historial de crédito.

rules.requirement: Starting July 1, 2024, most landlords may charge a security deposit of no more than one month's rent, whether the unit is furnished or not. Small landlords who are individuals (or family trusts or LLCs of individuals) owning no more than two rental properties with four or fewer units total may charge up to two months' rent.

Los pequeños propietarios que son personas (o fideicomisos familiares o LLC de personas) y que poseen no más de dos propiedades de alquiler con cuatro unidades o menos en total pueden cobrar hasta dos meses de renta.

rules.title: Security deposit cap
rules.requirement: A landlord may not ask for a security deposit of more than one month's rent, on top of the first month's rent. Small landlords (natural persons owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units) may ask for up to two months' rent, but not from service members.

Landlords who are natural persons (or LLCs whose members are all natural persons) owning no more than two residential rental properties with no more than four units total may collect up to two months' rent, except from service members. Does not apply to security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024. An advance payment of at least six months' rent is allowed for leases of six months or longer.

rules.quoted_span: (1) Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.
rules.requirement_es: El arrendador no puede pedir un depósito de garantía de más de un mes de renta, además de la renta del primer mes. Los arrendadores pequeños (personas naturales que tienen no más de dos propiedades de alquiler con no más de cuatro unidades) pueden pedir hasta dos meses de renta, pero no a miembros del servicio militar.

rules.title: Massachusetts statewide ban on local rent control
rules.requirement: Massachusetts cities and towns may not enact or enforce rent control. A city that accepts this law may only adopt voluntary rent control that cannot regulate evictions, cannot cover owners of fewer than ten units or units with fair market rent above $400, and must compensate owners from city funds.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies statewide to all cities and towns in Massachusetts.

rules.quoted_span: Section 4. No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides:
rules.conflict_note: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except narrow voluntary regulation in a city that accepts chapter 40P.; Any permitted local rent control regulation may not include the regulation of evictions.

Una ciudad que acepte esta ley solo puede adoptar un control de rentas voluntario que no puede regular los desalojos, no puede cubrir a dueños de menos de diez unidades ni unidades con renta de mercado mayor de $400, y debe compensar a los dueños con fondos municipales.

rules.title: Ban on source-of-income discrimination in rentals
rules.requirement: Landlords in Massachusetts may not discriminate against a renter because the renter receives public assistance or a housing subsidy, such as a rental voucher, or because of the requirements of that assistance program.

rules.title: Massachusetts security deposit limit and protections
rules.requirement: In Massachusetts, a security deposit cannot be more than one month's rent. The landlord must give receipts, keep it in a separate interest-bearing bank account in Massachusetts, pay you interest, and return it within 30 days after you move out, minus only allowed deductions.

rules.requirement_es: En Massachusetts, el depósito de seguridad no puede ser mayor que la renta de un mes. El propietario debe darle recibos, guardarlo en una cuenta bancaria separada con intereses en Massachusetts, pagarle intereses y devolverlo dentro de 30 días después de que usted se mude, menos solo las deducciones permitidas.

rules.title: Prohibition Against Algorithmic Rent-Fixing in the Rental Housing Market
rules.requirement: Landlords in Hoboken may not use software, algorithms, or data-sharing platforms that collect private information from competing landlords to coordinate, recommend, or set rents, lease terms, or occupancy levels.

coverage_conditions.text: Any residential dwelling unit in Hoboken, defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities.

exemptions.label: Medical/long-term care or detention facilities

all.source_text: Medical/long-term care or detention facility

rules.exemptions: Medical/long-term care or detention facilities
rules.quoted_span: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit (defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities) in the City of Hoboken are prohibited from price fixing using algorithmic pricing.
rules.conflict_note: may be preempted by P.L.2026, c.43 (FAIR Act), section 4
rules.requirement_es: Los propietarios en Hoboken no pueden usar programas, algoritmos o plataformas de intercambio de datos que recopilen información privada de otros propietarios competidores para coordinar, recomendar o fijar alquileres, términos de contrato o niveles de ocupación.

rules.title: Preventing Algorithmic Rent Fixing in the Rental Housing Market
rules.requirement: Landlords, their agents, and subcontractors in Jersey City may not subscribe to, contract with, pay for, or use the services of an algorithmic rent-setting service provider. Service providers may not help landlords agree not to compete on rents, fees, or other rental terms.

coverage_conditions.text: Real estate lessors, agents, or subcontractors in Jersey City, and service providers.

rules.quoted_span:
It is unlawful for any real estate lessor, agent, or subcontractor thereof, to subscribe to, contract with, or
      otherwise exchange anything of value in return for or otherwise utilize the services of a Service
      Provider.
rules.conflict_note: may be preempted by P.L.2026, c.43 (FAIR Act), section 4
rules.requirement_es: Los propietarios, sus agentes y subcontratistas en Jersey City no pueden suscribirse, contratar, pagar ni usar los servicios de un proveedor de fijación algorítmica de alquileres. Los proveedores de servicios no pueden ayudar a los propietarios a acordar no competir en alquileres, cargos u otros términos de alquiler.

rules.title: Jersey City Rent Control Ordinance
rules.requirement: Jersey City regulates rents under its Rent Control Ordinance, enforced by the Office of Landlord/Tenant Relations. Buildings with 1 to 4 units are exempt from rent control.

coverage_conditions.text: Rental properties in Jersey City subject to the Rent Control Ordinance (Chapter 260); 1-4 unit properties are exempt and other exemptions may be requested.

exemptions.label: 1-4 unit properties

rules.exemptions: 1-4 unit properties
rules.quoted_span: Please Note: All 1-4 Unit Properties are exempt from rent control
rules.requirement_es: Jersey City regula las rentas bajo su Ordenanza de Control de Rentas, aplicada por la Oficina de Relaciones entre Arrendadores e Inquilinos. Los edificios de 1 a 4 unidades están exentos del control de rentas.

rules.title: FAIR Act ban on algorithmic rent coordination
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot pay for or use rent-setting software or services that pool private data from competing landlords to set or recommend rents, and no one may coordinate rent prices this way. Violations are treated as breaking the New Jersey Antitrust Act.

coverage_conditions.text: Rental property owners, coordinators (operators of algorithmic revenue management software or algorithmic devices performing a coordinating function) and their agents, for residential dwelling units in New Jersey.

rules.quoted_span:
It
shall be unlawful and a violation of the “New Jersey Antitrust Act,” P.L.1970,
c.73 (C.56:9-1 et seq.) for:
a.     a rental property owner, or any agent,
representative, or subcontractor thereof, to receive, subscribe to, contract
for, or otherwise exchange any form of consideration in return for the use of,
the services of a coordinator;
rules.conflict_note: Municipalities are prohibited from enacting ordinances that conflict with the act.
rules.requirement_es: Los propietarios no pueden pagar ni usar programas o servicios que combinen datos privados de propietarios competidores para fijar o recomendar alquileres, y nadie puede coordinar precios de alquiler de esta forma. Las infracciones se tratan como violaciones de la Ley Antimonopolio de Nueva Jersey.

rules.title: Rental application fee cap
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent cannot charge more than $50 for a rental application fee. The cap goes up each year with inflation.

coverage_conditions.text: Applications to lease or sublease residential rental property, except units in one- or two-family dwellings and real estate licensees who are not the landlord.

exemptions.label: Unit in a one-family or two-family dwelling
Real estate licensee who is not the landlord

all.source_text: fee charged by a New Jersey Real Estate Commission licensee who is not the landlord

rules.exemptions: Unit in a one-family or two-family dwelling; Real estate licensee who is not the landlord
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord, or
agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply
to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which
exceeds $50.
rules.requirement_es: Un propietario o su agente no puede cobrar más de $50 por la solicitud de alquiler. El límite se ajusta cada año según la inflación.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act good-cause requirement
rules.requirement: A landlord can only evict a tenant or refuse to renew a lease (written or oral) for one of the good causes listed in state law, and must prove the cause in court. Except for unpaid rent, the landlord must give the tenant a written Notice to Quit describing the cause.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to most residential rentals, including single-family homes, mobile homes and mobile home park land, apartment buildings, complexes, and rooming and boarding homes. Does not apply to owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units, transient or seasonal hotel/motel/guest house occupants, or a unit held in trust for a developmentally disabled immediate family member who permanently occupies it.

exemptions.label: Owner-occupied two- or three-unit premises with two or fewer rental units

all.source_text: owner occupies one of the units

all.source_text: hotel, motel or guest house rented to a transient guest or seasonal tenant (not a continual resident with no alternate residence)

rules.quoted_span:
No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a 
lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause.
rules.requirement_es: El arrendador solo puede desalojar a un inquilino o negarse a renovar un contrato (escrito u oral) por una de las causas justificadas que indica la ley estatal, y debe probar la causa ante el tribunal. Excepto por falta de pago del alquiler, el arrendador debe darle al inquilino un Aviso de Desalojo (Notice to Quit) por escrito que describa la causa.

rules.title: No state rent control; increases must not be unconscionable
rules.requirement: New Jersey has no statewide cap on rent. A landlord cannot raise rent in the middle of a lease, must give proper written notice to end the old lease and offer a new one, and the increase cannot be unconscionable (shockingly unfair) and must follow any local rent control ordinance.
rules.key_value: No fixed cap; increase must not be unconscionable

coverage_conditions.text: Applies statewide to tenancies covered by the Anti-Eviction Act. Local rent control or rent leveling ordinances may set stricter limits; newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control for 30 years after completion (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5), and HUD- or NJHMFA-controlled housing is not subject to municipal rent control.

rules.quoted_span:
The increase in rent must not be 
unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest 
person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.
rules.requirement_es: Nueva Jersey no tiene un límite estatal sobre el alquiler. El arrendador no puede subir el alquiler a mitad del contrato, debe dar aviso por escrito para terminar el contrato anterior y ofrecer uno nuevo, y el aumento no puede ser abusivo (injusto de manera escandalosa) y debe cumplir con cualquier ordenanza local de control de alquileres.

rules.title: Source of income discrimination ban
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot turn you down or treat you differently because of how you pay rent, such as a Section 8 voucher or other lawful income.

coverage_conditions.text: Rental of all property, except a unit in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling and rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling.

The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination  based

rules.requirement_es: Los propietarios no pueden rechazarlo ni tratarlo de forma diferente por la manera en que paga el alquiler, como con un vale de la Sección 8 u otro ingreso legal.

rules.title: Law Against Discrimination: source of lawful income
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot refuse to rent to you or treat you differently because of your source of lawful income (such as housing vouchers or benefits), or because of race, religion, disability, familial status, and other protected traits.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to all landlord-tenant relationships except two-family owner-occupied dwellings, rooms in an owner- or resident-occupied single home, and single-sex residences (and age-restricted housing as to familial status).

exemptions.label: Two-family owner-occupied dwelling

all.source_text: owner occupies one of the units

room rented in owner- or resident-occupied home

rules.exemptions: Two-family owner-occupied dwelling; Room in an owner- or resident-occupied single-family home
rules.quoted_span:
The New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD), 
N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) to -(h), prohibits discrimination when selling or renting property and requires 
equal treatment in the sale or rental of housing regardless of race, creed, color, national origin, 
ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, 
affectional or sexual orientation, gender  identity or expression, mental and physical disability, 
nationality, or source of lawful income.
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores no pueden negarse a alquilarle ni tratarle de manera diferente por la fuente de sus ingresos legales (como vales de vivienda o beneficios), ni por raza, religión, discapacidad, situación familiar y otras características protegidas.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act: criminal history screening limits
rules.requirement: In New Jersey, a landlord cannot ask about your criminal record until after making you a conditional offer to rent. After that, they can only consider certain recent or serious convictions, must do an individual review, and must tell you in writing why if they take back the offer.
rules.key_value: No criminal-history inquiry before conditional offer; lookback 6 yrs (1st degree), 4 yrs (2nd/3rd degree), 1 yr (4th degree)

coverage_conditions.text: Rental dwelling units offered by housing providers, other than units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units. Exceptions allow considering methamphetamine production on federally assisted housing premises and lifetime sex offender registration.

all.source_text: owner occupies the premises

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises of not more than four units
rules.quoted_span:
A housing
provider

rules.requirement_es: En Nueva Jersey, el propietario no puede preguntar sobre sus antecedentes penales hasta después de hacerle una oferta condicional de alquiler. Después, solo puede considerar ciertas condenas recientes o graves, debe hacer una evaluación individual y debe explicarle por escrito si retira la oferta.

rules.title: Security deposit limit (Security Deposit Law)
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot collect a security deposit of more than one and a half times one month's rent. Any yearly increase in the deposit cannot be more than 10% of the current deposit, and the deposit must be returned with interest, minus allowed deductions, within 30 days after the tenancy ends.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes. Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless the tenant sends a written request to have the law apply (effective 30 days after the request).

exemptions.label: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling (unless tenant opts in by written request)

all.source_text: owner occupies one of the units

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling (unless tenant opts in by written request)
rules.quoted_span:
The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than 
one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ).
rules.requirement_es: El arrendador no puede cobrar un depósito de seguridad de más de una vez y media el alquiler de un mes. Cualquier aumento anual del depósito no puede superar el 10% del depósito actual, y el depósito debe devolverse con intereses, menos las deducciones permitidas, dentro de los 30 días después de que termine el arrendamiento.
